table.ruleA: 6 tiers; budget/heat/cool = (10,7,3),(8,6,2),(12,9,4),(6,5,2),(9,7,3),(7,5,2); start 3,6,6,2,2,1; all COLD; limit 38; drop count 0; every division rounded down; identical 5x6 ingest schedule
table.ruleB: 6 compartments; volume/inception/desinence identical; start 3,6,6,2,2,1; all LAMINAR; blow limit 38; Total Overboard 0; quarters and halves rounded down; identical Fill Table

table.ruleA: Add the scheduled chunks to each tier; budget not enforced
table.ruleB: Add the fill amount to each compartment; volume not enforced

table.ruleA: Sequential 1 to 6; if count > budget, excess goes to tier n+1 (already there when n+1 is handled), count set to budget; at or below budget does nothing; excess from tier 6 is added to drop count
table.ruleB: Sequential 1 to 6; if contents > volume, excess goes aft to n+1 before n+1 is checked, contents set to volume; equal or less does nothing; excess from 6 goes overboard

table.ruleA: Read counts after step 2; COLD with count >= heat becomes HOT; HOT with count <= cool becomes COLD; otherwise unchanged; at most one change per cycle; log (cycle, tier, before, after)
table.ruleB: Read contents after Step 2; LAMINAR with contents >= inception becomes CAVITATING; CAVITATING with contents <= desinence becomes LAMINAR; otherwise unchanged; at most one change per cycle; log the same 4-tuple

table.ruleA: Compute all amounts from counts at the start of the step using post-step-3 state: COLD floor(count/4), HOT floor(count/2); then apply simultaneously; COLD amount dropped; HOT amount to tier n-1; HOT tier 1 amount dropped; budget not enforced
table.ruleB: Compute all amounts from contents at the start of the step: LAMINAR floor(contents/4), CAVITATING floor(contents/2); apply together; LAMINAR amount overboard; CAVITATING amount to n-1; compartment 1 backflow overboard; volume not enforced

table.ruleA: Sum of six counts > 38 fires the reset (exactly 38 does not); log the cycle
table.ruleB: Sum of six contents > 38 fires the blow (exactly 38 does not); log the cycle

table.ruleA: Only HOT tiers are halved (floor(count/2)); COLD tiers are left as they are; removed chunks go to drop count
table.ruleB: Every compartment is halved (floor(contents/2)) regardless of pump state; removed units go overboard
table.difference: A halves only HOT positions and keeps COLD positions whole; B halves all six positions including LAMINAR (COLD) ones. Any COLD/LAMINAR position holding 1 or more at a firing changes the outcome.

table.ruleA: (a) end counts 1-6, (b) end states, (c) all state changes in order, (d) reset cycles, (e) final drop count, (f) balance check
table.ruleB: (a) end contents 1-6, (b) end pump states, (c) all pump state changes, (d) blow cycles or none, (e) Total Overboard, (f) balance check

result.probeWhy: The suspected difference is which positions the line-wide halving covers, so the probe has to fire the halving while at least one COLD/LAMINAR position holds 1 or more, and must not let later cycles erase the gap. Cycle 1 by hand: after ingest [6,7,15,0,9,11]; eviction gives [6,7,12,3,9,7] and drops 4; positions 2,3,5,6 go HOT while 1 and 4 stay COLD; compaction/promotion gives [8,10,6,7,8,4] (drop count 5), total 43 > 38, so the halving fires. A halves only the HOT positions: [8,5,3,7,4,2], drop count 19. B halves everything: [4,5,3,3,4,2], drop count 27. Inputs in cycles 2-5 are all zero, so nothing refills the line and the gap reaches the end report. Why the printed tables hide it: the printed run does diverge after the cycle 1 halving (COLD positions 1 and 6 hold 7 and 3; A keeps them, B halves them to 3 and 1), and the mid-run counts differ through cycle 3. But by the cycle 4 firing every position is HOT and budget clipping has absorbed the gap, so the two runs reconverge exactly ([4,5,4,3,4,2], tally 74 for both after cycle 4). Their printed end reports are therefore identical, a coincidence of those tables. A random search over 20,000 start/input pairs (digits 0-9) found 4,604 where the end reports differ.
result.differingRule: At step 5, when the total is above 38, A halves only the HOT tiers and leaves the COLD tiers whole, while B halves all six compartments whatever their pump state.
result.trust: Both routes agree on DIFFERENT. Route 1 finds the step 5 halving-scope rule as the only differing clause; every other step matches clause by clause, including the order, the rounding targets, the inclusive and strict thresholds, where amounts go, and the strict > 38 trigger. Route 2 shows it in practice: the probe fires one halving while positions 1 and 4 are COLD/LAMINAR and holding 8 and 7, and the end reports differ in quantities (A 2,2,6,2,3,2 vs B 3,2,4,2,2,2), state changes, and loss tally (31 vs 33). The printed tables produce identical end reports (both 6,10,9,7,4,2, halving in cycles 1 and 4, tally 76, balance 114 = 114), but only because the runs reconverge. They diverge after cycle 1, where COLD positions 1 and 6 hold 7 and 3 at the firing, and become identical again by the cycle 4 firing, when all six positions are HOT and clipping has absorbed the gap. A check on the printed tables alone would wrongly say SAME. I used a Python script for the arithmetic (C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-fm\P16\sim.py, with search.py, search2.py and search3.py for probe search) and checked probe cycle 1 by hand. Balance holds in every run: probe 54 = 54 for A (23 end + 31 tally) and for B (21 end + 33 tally).
